tagline: The virtual K-pop debut that became League's most-watched video.
headline: Four champions became pop stars at Worlds 2018, and their debut remains the most-viewed video on League's YouTube channel.
summary: On November 3, 2018, Riot Games unveiled K/DA (Ahri, Akali, Evelynn and Kai'Sa, voiced by Miyeon and Soyeon of (G)I-DLE, Madison Beer and Jaira Burns) with a live performance of POP/STARS beside augmented-reality versions of the champions before the Worlds final in Incheon. Fortiche's music video passed 100 million views within a month, and the song topped Billboard's World Digital Song Sales chart before later going Platinum in the US. In April 2019 the video overtook Warriors as the most-viewed upload on the League of Legends channel; on October 13, 2026 it stands at 668.2 million views, about 211 million ahead of anything else there, and the band it launched paved the way for True Damage, K/DA's 2020 comeback and HEARTSTEEL.

story.heading: A one-off for Worlds in Korea
story.body:
In 2018 the World Championship went back to South Korea, and Riot wanted the finals to have more than an anthem. Viranda Tantula, creative lead on the Worlds opening ceremony and music, told Variety the goal was a "dope 'League' moment" for players. The champions were going to step into the real world, and he said the song and the show had to hold up against real pop songs and real performances. K/DA was planned as a one-off, and nobody was planning beyond that night.

The lineup followed the archetypes of a pop group. Ahri was the obvious leader. She continued the Pop Star Ahri skin from 2013, and the team felt a show in Korea needed the original pop star, a champion with strong ties to the Korean community. Evelynn became the provocative diva. Akali, who was being reworked at the time, became the rebellious rapper. Kai'Sa became the quiet loner who expresses herself through dance. Skins lead Janelle Jimenez joked that the group was "Ahri and the New Girls", because the other three champions were new or had just been reworked. About 100 people worked on the full package: skins, song, video, publishing and even dancing minions.

story.heading: Writing a bilingual banger
story.body:
Riot composer Sebastien Najand wrote *POP/STARS* with songwriter Harloe, Justin Tranter was an executive producer, and Lydia Paek and Minji Kim translated the Korean lines. Najand told Dot Esports that the first demo was entirely in English. The team then tried versions with more Korean, because they wanted a real mix of Western pop and K-pop, not the usual K-pop format of mostly Korean with a few English lines. The English chorus was strong enough that they kept it. For sound, they looked to Cube Entertainment's harder-hitting songs, especially 4Minute, and aimed for a busier arrangement than minimalist Western pop.

Cube was the first K-pop company Riot met with, and several people on the team were already fans of (G)I-DLE. Soyeon was chosen for the rap and Miyeon for Ahri's voice, while Madison Beer and Jaira Burns sang Evelynn and Kai'Sa. Riot Music Group head Toa Dunn said the song was written around the characters, with a rap section for Akali and the pre-chorus for Ahri. The singers also did motion capture for their characters. Miyeon told Billboard she played League as Ahri to understand her, and Soyeon said she tried to move the way Akali would.

story.heading: Incheon, November 3, 2018
story.body:
The band debuted before the final at Incheon Munhak Stadium, where Invictus Gaming beat Fnatic for the title. A neon countdown introduced the members one by one. Then Madison Beer, Jaira Burns, Miyeon and Soyeon performed live while AR versions of Ahri, Akali, Evelynn and Kai'Sa danced next to them. The AR characters appeared on the stadium screens and on the stream as if they were on the stage. Tantula told Dot Esports that a virtual performer can do things no human can, like Ahri flying onto the stage, but that Riot still wanted the live singers there for the ad-libs and live expressions a virtual performer can't yet give.

The final had 99.6 million unique viewers and a peak of 44 million concurrent viewers, so K/DA's first show reached one of the biggest audiences esports had ever drawn. The Verge's Julia Alexander called the performance incredible to watch and the song an absolute jam. The official upload of the ceremony performance now has about 66 million views.

story.heading: Fortiche's neon subway
story.body:
The music video was released on the League of Legends channel the same day. Fortiche, the Paris studio that had made Riot's Pentakill video and later animated *Arcane*, produced it. Video creative lead Patrick Morales said he wanted K/DA to live somewhere between fantasy and reality, so the characters have a cartoonish, almost hand-drawn look against realistic backgrounds. Director Arnaud pitched a visual gimmick for each member. Akali's started as neon spray paint and graffiti, her mask's teeth were inspired by *dokkaebi*, Korean goblins, and the team then decided to tag Akali herself as well as the subway. That scene became the one most people remember. Riot's own award entry says its popularity led the team to cover Akali's in-game event skin in graffiti too.

The video also hides details for Korean viewers: pink subway seats suggested by Riot's Korean office, Hangul adverts for Pizza Delivery Sivir and a lost Pug'maw, a Lux skincare line, Ahri's finger heart and the laundromat, a common K-pop video setting.

story.heading: Records from day one
story.body:
The video had about 5 million views in its first 24 hours, which Fox Sports Asia reported as the biggest 24-hour start for a K-pop group's debut video at the time. The previous record of about 4.5 million belonged to IZ*ONE's *La Vie en Rose*. The video reached 13 million views in 48 hours and 20 million in four days, which Riot said was a better start than any other League music video. It passed 100 million within a month. Riot's award entry adds that it was the most-viewed Riot video ever over its first 2, 7 and 14 days.

The song charted too. It entered Billboard's World Digital Song Sales chart at No. 1 after selling 9,000 copies in its first week. That was the first No. 1 on the chart for Madison Beer, (G)I-DLE and Jaira Burns, and it made (G)I-DLE only the fourth K-pop girl group to top it. It also went to No. 1 on Apple Music's US K-pop chart and No. 5 on its pop chart. Billboard's Jeff Benjamin wrote that esports might start to shape what becomes a hit. The RIAA certified the song Platinum in August 2022, and by October 2026 it had more than 434 million Spotify streams.

story.heading: The fandom takes over
story.body:
Fan art and cosplay spread quickly. The Verge noted that Akali, not Ahri, became the most-drawn member, and her rap scene with Evelynn started a popular fan pairing of the two. Many fans said they had quit League years earlier, or had never played it, and joined in because the video looked so cool. Players ground through in-game missions to earn the Prestige Kai'Sa skin, and started putting the four K/DA champions on one team with Taric, cast as the band's manager. Riot's team said the joke came entirely from the community. Morales said the YouTube comment he saw most was some version of "normally not into League/K-pop/gaming, but K/DA is the exception".

The song soon showed up outside League. It was a free download in *Beat Saber* that December, the first time a League song officially appeared in a rhythm game. In April 2019 most of Cloud9's League roster dressed up as K/DA, and in 2021 *Just Dance 2022* put POP/STARS on its main tracklist.

story.heading: Dethroning Warriors
story.body:
Imagine Dragons' *Warriors* had been the most-viewed video on the League of Legends channel for years. In April 2019, five months after release, POP/STARS passed it with about 215 million views to 214 million.

A check of the full channel on October 13, 2026 (all 1,560 videos, 260 Shorts and 6 live streams) shows POP/STARS still at No. 1 with 668.2 million views and 6.4 million likes. That is about 211 million more than *Warriors* (457.2M), with *RISE* (425.3M), *Enemy* (370.1M) and the *Legends Never Die* music video (317.9M) next. No other upload on the channel has more than 457.2 million views.

story.heading: The blueprint for Riot's virtual bands
story.body:
POP/STARS won the Games category at the 11th Shorty Awards and was a finalist for Best Original Song at the 2019 G.A.N.G. Awards. It also showed what Riot's music ambitions could achieve. Tantula told Billboard that Riot was building an in-house music team with the services of a regular record label, including distribution, A&R and promotion. The next year Akali got a second band, the hip-hop group True Damage, with Soyeon voicing her again at the Worlds 2019 final in Paris. K/DA returned in 2020 with *THE BADDEST*, *MORE* and the *ALL OUT* EP, and performed *MORE* at the Worlds 2020 final in Shanghai, where Riot used more than four times as many AR tracking cameras as it had in 2018. In 2023 Riot launched HEARTSTEEL, which American Songwriter described as Riot riding the wave of K/DA's success. In 2026 True Damage sings the Worlds anthem, *Know My Name*.

The singers kept the song alive as well. (G)I-DLE, now styled i-dle, covered POP/STARS at a 2020 online concert, put it on the setlist of their 2022 world tour, and were still performing it on their Syncopation World Tour in 2026. Fans haven't given up on K/DA either. In 2026 an ASCAP registration for a K/DA song called *WATCH ME*, with Najand among its writers, started talk of a comeback, although Riot hasn't confirmed one.

whyItMatters: It is the most-viewed video on the League of Legends YouTube channel: 668.2M views on October 13, 2026, about 211M more than Warriors, the video it replaced at No. 1 in April 2019.
It turned a skin line into a real pop act: No. 1 on Billboard's World Digital Song Sales, RIAA Platinum, and more than 434M Spotify streams.
Its AR debut at the Worlds 2018 final, seen by 99.6M unique viewers, put a fictional band on one of the biggest stages in esports.
It reached people who weren't League fans: lapsed and new players, K-pop fans, fan artists and cosplayers, and later Beat Saber and Just Dance.
It became the model for Riot's virtual bands: True Damage (2019), K/DA's ALL OUT comeback (2020), HEARTSTEEL (2023), and True Damage singing the Worlds anthem in 2026.
Its singers are still part of the story: Soyeon came back as Akali in True Damage, and (G)I-DLE/i-dle were still performing POP/STARS on tour in 2026.

communityMoments.title: K/DA debuts in AR at the Worlds final
communityMoments.description: Madison Beer, Jaira Burns, Miyeon and Soyeon performed POP/STARS next to AR versions of Ahri, Akali, Evelynn and Kai'Sa at Incheon Munhak Stadium before the Invictus Gaming vs. Fnatic final. Ahri flew in with all nine tails spread.

communityMoments.title: A 24-hour record
communityMoments.description: The music video got about 5 million views in its first day, which Fox Sports Asia reported as a record at the time for a K-pop group's debut video, ahead of IZ*ONE's La Vie en Rose.

communityMoments.title: Fan art takes over, and Akali steals the show
communityMoments.description: Fan art and cosplay spread quickly. Akali became the most-drawn member, her rap scene with Evelynn fuelled a popular pairing, and players who had quit League or never played said they were joining in.

communityMoments.title: Taric, band manager
communityMoments.description: Players started running all four K/DA champions on one team with Taric as their "manager". Riot's skins lead said the joke came entirely from the community.

communityMoments.title: No. 1 on Billboard
communityMoments.description: POP/STARS entered Billboard's World Digital Song Sales chart at No. 1 with 9,000 copies sold in its first week, the first No. 1 on that chart for all three acts.

communityMoments.title: 100 million views in a month
communityMoments.description: Riot Games Korea announced that the video had passed 100 million views less than a month after release.

communityMoments.title: Free in Beat Saber
communityMoments.description: POP/STARS was added to the VR rhythm game Beat Saber as a free download with an Expert+ map, the first time a League song officially appeared in a rhythm game.

communityMoments.title: Cloud9 suits up as K/DA
communityMoments.description: Cloud9's League roster dressed up as K/DA for a photoshoot: Svenskeren as Ahri, Sneaky as Akali, Licorice as Evelynn and Zeyzal as Kai'Sa.

communityMoments.title: POP/STARS overtakes Warriors
communityMoments.description: Five months after release, the video passed Imagine Dragons' Warriors (about 215M to 214M views) and became the most-viewed upload on the League of Legends channel.

communityMoments.title: Soyeon returns as Akali, now in True Damage
communityMoments.description: One year later Akali had a new group. Soyeon voiced her again in the hip-hop act True Damage, which performed at the Worlds 2019 final in Paris.

communityMoments.title: (G)I-DLE sing it as six
communityMoments.description: At their online concert I-Land: Who Am I, all six members of (G)I-DLE performed their own version of POP/STARS, with Soyeon on the rap.

communityMoments.title: K/DA back on the Worlds stage
communityMoments.description: K/DA returned for the Worlds 2020 final in Shanghai and performed MORE with Seraphine (Lexie Liu). The show used four times as many AR tracking cameras as 2018 and gave Akali a virtual Ducati.

communityMoments.title: On the Just Dance 2022 tracklist
communityMoments.description: Ubisoft's Just Dance 2022 put POP/STARS on its main tracklist as an exclusive collaboration with K/DA.

communityMoments.title: Certified Platinum
communityMoments.description: The RIAA certified POP/STARS Platinum in the United States.

communityMoments.title: Still on the setlist in 2026
communityMoments.description: i-dle (formerly styled (G)I-DLE) performed POP/STARS on their Syncopation World Tour, which opened in Seoul on February 21, 2026.

communityMoments.title: WATCH ME sparks comeback talk
communityMoments.description: An ASCAP entry for a K/DA song called WATCH ME, with POP/STARS composer Sebastien Najand among its writers, started talk of a comeback. Riot has not announced one.

keyMoments.label: Cold open
keyMoments.description: A silhouetted Evelynn sits on a supercar between blazing headlights as the intro hook starts.

keyMoments.label: K/DA on the departure board
keyMoments.description: A subway destination sign flips to the K/DA logo, then the four members appear in silhouette against bright windows.

keyMoments.label: Ahri's laundromat
keyMoments.description: Ahri lounges on a row of washing machines for the pre-chorus. The laundromat is one of the video's nods to K-pop video settings.

keyMoments.label: Akali tags the subway
keyMoments.description: The subway lights go out and the video switches to blacklight neon: graffiti, glowing sneakers and Akali's masked face.

keyMoments.label: First chorus drop
keyMoments.description: A neon graffiti dragon fills the screen, then all four members dance the chorus choreography on a dark stage.

keyMoments.label: Akali's rap
keyMoments.description: Akali's glowing grin fills the frame, then she launches into her rap (voiced by Soyeon) against a wall of neon K/DA graffiti.

keyMoments.label: Evelynn and Akali
keyMoments.description: Evelynn and Akali share a moment in the subway car. The Verge pointed to this rap scene as fuel for the Akali and Evelynn fan pairing.

keyMoments.label: Nine tails
keyMoments.description: Back in the laundromat, Ahri spreads her nine glowing tails.

keyMoments.label: Second chorus
keyMoments.description: After a flash of Akali in neon, the video cuts back to all four members for the second chorus choreography.

keyMoments.label: Bridge in the tunnel
keyMoments.description: The bridge slows things down. A neon outline and pink and blue light trails race through a subway tunnel, then Evelynn leans on a supercar in red light.

keyMoments.label: Final chorus: the white moon
keyMoments.description: Ahri appears against a huge white moon for the final chorus, and the others join her.

keyMoments.label: Violet and red discs
keyMoments.description: The members take turns in front of a giant violet disc and then a red one while laser lines sweep across the stage.

keyMoments.label: Final formation
keyMoments.description: Akali crouches front and centre while Evelynn, Ahri and Kai'Sa pose behind her under sweeping ribbon blades, before the K/DA logo appears.

keyMoments.label: The countdown
keyMoments.description: Each member appears inside a giant neon number as the stadium counts down to the debut.

keyMoments.label: The AR band walks out
keyMoments.description: After a Korean subway sign reading 'next station' flips to K/DA, the AR versions of Ahri, Akali, Evelynn and Kai'Sa walk out together onto the Worlds stage.

keyMoments.label: Akali's grin over the stadium
keyMoments.description: A wide shot shows Akali's neon grin filling the giant screen above the stage and the dancers.

keyMoments.label: Ahri takes flight
keyMoments.description: The AR version of Ahri rises above the stage with her nine tails spread, then lands among the dancers. Riot pointed to this as something no human performer could do.

featuredClip.description: Akali's glowing grin fills the frame, then she starts her rap against a wall of neon K/DA graffiti.
